subject: chemistry-1
question: An aluminum atom has 13 protons and 13 electrons. If it loses 3 electrons during a chemical reaction, which term and charge correctly describe the resulting particle?

options.text: An anion carrying a 3- charge, because removing electrons leaves the particle negative
An isotope carrying a 3+ charge, because the number of nuclear particles has changed
A cation carrying a 3+ charge, because protons now outnumber electrons by three
A cation carrying a 13+ charge, because all 13 protons are now unopposed

explanation:
Net ionic charge equals protons minus electrons: 13 - 10 = +3. A positively charged ion is a cation, and cations form by losing electrons. The 10 remaining electrons still cancel 10 of the 13 protons, so the charge is 3+, not 13+. Isotopes differ in neutron count, and the proton count (element identity) does not change in a chemical reaction, so the species is Al3+.

ELI-10: Charge is a subtraction problem, not a count of what is left. Protons are fixed at 13 and each one contributes +1; each electron contributes -1. Start at 13 plus and 13 minus, which cancel to zero. Remove 3 electrons and you have 13 plus against 10 minus, so 10 pairs cancel and 3 pluses survive: a 3+ charge. Any positively charged ion is a cation (the 't' in cation is a handy stand-in for a plus sign), and losing electrons is the only way an atom becomes one.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
